name: Oklahoma
note: In Oklahoma the funeral director files the death certificate electronically with the State Department of Health. The consolidated statutes carry conflicting versions of the filing deadline: three days after death in two 2025 versions, ten days in a 2024 version. The certifier has 48 hours (or five days after receiving the partial record). Every death leading to cremation goes through the Chief Medical Examiner's permit. Registration fans out by statute: monthly to the State Election Board (county boards must purge within 30 days), quarterly to the Department of Public Safety to cancel driver licences, monthly to the Health Care Authority to end Medicaid enrollment, and to the Department of Veterans Affairs and DHS. Certified copies are restricted. The Department may run electronic death verification for government agencies, life insurers, annuity companies, pension plans and fraud-prevention entities, and death data enter a free online public index after five years.

steps.title: Declare death under accepted medical standards
steps.who: The person declaring death (the profession is not named). All reasonable attempts to restore circulation or respiration must be made first.
steps.trigger: Irreversible cessation of circulatory and respiratory functions, or of all brain functions.
steps.summary: Oklahoma's version of the Uniform Determination of Death Act adds a duty to try resuscitation before declaring death.

steps.title: Notify the medical examiner of reportable deaths
steps.who: Law enforcement and other officials, the attending physician, or other persons if no physician attended. Heads of state hospitals and institutions must report every death of a patient, inmate, ward or veteran before releasing the body.
steps.trigger: Violent, suspicious or unnatural deaths, public-health threats, unattended deaths, deaths in custody, maternal deaths, and every body to be cremated, taken out of state or otherwise made unavailable for study.
steps.summary: The Office of the Chief Medical Examiner investigates the listed death types. Bodies may not be disturbed until it authorises.

steps.title: Medical examiner certifies investigated deaths
steps.who: The Chief Medical Examiner or designee.
steps.trigger: A death investigated under 63 O.S. § 931 ff. The State Registrar may also refer a physician's certificate for ME investigation.

deadline.text: immediately on conclusion of the investigation

steps.summary: Only a medical examiner death certificate signed by the Chief Medical Examiner or designee is valid in these cases.

steps.title: Next of kin supply personal data to the funeral director
steps.who: The next of kin or the best qualified person or source available.
steps.summary: The funeral director must warn that knowingly giving false data or misrepresenting a relationship to the decedent is a felony (Class D3).

steps.title: Funeral director sends the partial certificate to the certifier
steps.who: The funeral director, to the physician, PA, APRN or medical examiner who will complete the medical certification.
steps.trigger: Entry of personal data in the electronic system.

deadline.text: within twenty-four hours after the death

steps.summary: All versions of 63 O.S. § 1-317 require the partial certificate to reach the certifier within 24 hours of death.

steps.title: Certifier enters and signs the medical certification electronically
steps.who: The physician, PA or APRN in charge of care, or the one in attendance at death, or the hospice medical director.

deadline.text: within forty-eight hours after death (versions 2 and 3); within five calendar days after receipt (version 1)

steps.summary: Physicians have had to certify in the electronic system since 1 July 2017.

steps.title: Funeral director files the death certificate with the State Department of Health
steps.who: The funeral director, or the person acting as such who first assumed custody of the body.

deadline.text: within three days after death (2025 versions); ten calendar days (2024 version)

steps.summary: Funeral directors have had to sign and file in the prescribed electronic system since 1 July 2012. Under the 2024 version, the funeral director does a final review and submits within four days of the medical certification.

steps.title: Chief Medical Examiner's permit before cremation or burial at sea
steps.who: The person legally responsible for disposition applies. The funeral director files the original application-permit with the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner.
steps.trigger: A decision to cremate, bury at sea, or otherwise make the body unavailable for pathologic study.

deadline.text: filed or postmarked within forty-eight hours of the death

steps.summary: The medical examiner must investigate, issue a valid death certificate and execute a numbered permit. A copy of the permit and the original certificate go to the State Department of Health.

steps.title: Certified copies to listed persons only
steps.who: The State Department of Health. Eligible: the subject, parents, persons with the subject's permission, estate or probate representatives, estate attorneys (by affidavit), court-order holders, prosecutors, funeral directors (death certificates only), DOC and DHS, and others in the subject's best interest as defined by rule.
steps.summary: Disclosure outside the list is unlawful. Death certificates become public 50 years after the death.

steps.title: Monthly death list to the State Election Board
steps.who: The State Department of Health, to the Secretary of the State Election Board, who passes it to county election boards.
steps.trigger: Deaths of residents in the preceding month.

deadline.text: monthly; county board removes the voter within thirty days of receipt

steps.summary: The list includes name, dates of birth and death, and, where held, the last four SSN digits and the driver licence or ID number. The Election Board also matches against SSA and other states' death records.

steps.title: Quarterly death list to the Department of Public Safety to cancel driver licences
steps.who: The State Department of Health, to the Department of Public Safety.

deadline.text: at the end of each quarter year

steps.summary: DPS must use the list to update its records and cancel the licence of each deceased holder. Motor-vehicle-collision deaths are also reported monthly for statistics.

steps.title: Monthly death list to the Oklahoma Health Care Authority
steps.who: The State Department of Health, to the Oklahoma Health Care Authority (Medicaid).
steps.trigger: Registered deaths of residents in the preceding month.
steps.summary: The OHCA must identify deceased participants and end their Medicaid enrollment.

steps.title: Veteran deaths to the Oklahoma Department of Veterans Affairs
steps.who: The State Department of Health, to the Oklahoma Department of Veterans Affairs.
steps.trigger: Registered deaths where the record shows veteran status.
steps.summary: The list (name, SSN, date of death, place of interment) maintains the state veterans registry.

steps.title: Death data to the Department of Human Services
steps.who: The State Department of Health, to the Oklahoma Department of Human Services, under a data sharing agreement.
steps.trigger: Registered deaths relevant to DHS programmes.
steps.summary: Death data are sent electronically to support DHS-administered programmes. DHS may not release them under the Open Records Act.

steps.title: Funeral director, nursing home or family notifies the county election board
steps.who: A funeral director (notarised or witnessed form), a nursing facility or State Veterans Home administrator, next of kin (prescribed form), or anyone presenting a certified copy.
steps.trigger: The death of a registered voter.
steps.summary: The county election board secretary may cancel the registration on any of these notices.

steps.title: Electronic death verification for insurers, pension plans and fraud prevention
steps.who: The State Department of Health (or its contractor), for government agencies, benefit-paying parties (annuity companies, pension plans, life insurers), physicians checking lost-to-care patients, and other entities for fraud protection once their purpose is verified.
steps.summary: The Department may verify that a death certificate exists for legal and administrative purposes at any time after death, for up to $4 per check. Recipients may not pass the result on.

steps.title: Free online public death index after five years

deadline.text: death data added five years after the death

steps.summary: The index gives name, gender, dates of birth and death, and county of death. Private entities may request bulk digital files at cost.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: The consolidated statutes carry three versions of 63 O.S. § 1-317. Versions 2 and 3 (Laws 2025, c. 58 and c. 343) say three days after death. Version 1 (SB 707, Laws 2024, c. 251) says ten calendar days. The shortest is recorded.

informantDuty.note: The funeral director personally signs and files. Next of kin supply personal data.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review of every certificate. The Chief Medical Examiner investigates the 63 O.S. § 938 categories, which include every body to be cremated or taken out of state, and the State Registrar may refer any physician's certificate for investigation.

electronicRegistration.note: Electronic filing has been mandatory for funeral directors since 1 July 2012 and for physicians since 1 July 2017.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No population register. The State Department of Health keeps an event register with an online index.

governmentPropagation.note: Registration alone sends deaths by statute to the State Election Board (monthly), the Department of Public Safety (quarterly, licence cancellation), the Oklahoma Health Care Authority (monthly, Medicaid termination), the Department of Veterans Affairs and DHS. State tax is not covered. Federal feeds are in the us-federal layer.

certificateAccess.note: Copies only to the listed persons (subject, parents, estate representatives, estate attorneys, funeral directors, court-order holders and others). Death certificates become public after 50 years. A name-and-date index is public after 5 years.

privateSectorVerification.note: There is a statutory electronic death-verification route for benefit-paying parties (annuity companies, pension plans, life insurers) and fraud-prevention entities, at up to $4 per check.

gaps: 63 O.S. § 1-317 appears in three versions in the consolidated Title 63 PDF: v1 (SB 707, Laws 2024, c. 251) with a 10-day deadline, and v2 (HB 1688, Laws 2025, c. 58) and v3 (HB 2584, Laws 2025, c. 343) with a 3-day deadline. Which controls was not resolved. The enrolled bills were not read.
The title PDFs on oklegislature.gov are a consolidated snapshot (DER notes Last-Modified 31 December 2025). Amendments from the 2026 session would not appear.
oscn.net (section-level statute pages) sits behind a Cloudflare Turnstile and was not used. All citations point to the whole-title PDFs, so pinpoints are in the cite text.
Who may pronounce death (e.g. hospice nurses) was not traced. 63 O.S. § 3122 is profession-neutral.
No statutory feed to the Oklahoma Tax Commission was found. Title 68 was not searched.

Driver licences now appear to be handled by Service Oklahoma (26 O.S. § 4-120(A)(7) refers to surrendering a licence 'to Service Oklahoma'), but 63 O.S. § 1-323(E) still names the Department of Public Safety. The step follows the statute text.
Whether Oklahoma sends deaths to SSA through electronic death registration is not stated in Title 63. That is left to the us-federal layer.
